intro.en: The people and the parts of a newspaper, kinds of press, and how to talk about how reliable the news is.

texto.en:
**The paper.** **La portada** carries **los titulares**. Inside: **noticias**, **crónicas** (an account by someone who was there), **reportajes**, **entrevistas**, **artículos de opinión**, **el editorial** (the paper's own view), **cartas al director**, **críticas** de cine. Under a photo there is **un pie de foto**.

**The people.** **El redactor** writes in **la redacción**. **El corresponsal** lives abroad; **el enviado especial** is sent for one story. **El reportero**, **el cámara**, **el locutor**, **el presentador**.

**Kinds of press.** **La prensa escrita** and **la prensa digital**; **deportiva**, **económica**, **gratuita**. **La prensa rosa** or **del corazón** deals with famous people's lives. **La prensa amarilla** is sensationalist.

**The public.** **Los lectores**, **los oyentes** (radio), **los telespectadores**. Together they are **la audiencia**, and a programme **tiene mucha audiencia**. You **te suscribes a** un periódico. In front of the television you **zapeas**.

**True or not.** **Una noticia fiable**, **oficial**, **de última hora**. **Un rumor.** **Un bulo** (a hoax). **Según fuentes** del ministerio… A government **confirma** or **desmiente** a story.

**Freedom.** **La libertad de prensa** and **la libertad de expresión**, against **la censura**.

**Verbs of saying** in the news: **declarar**, **anunciar**, **afirmar**, **comunicar**, **comentar**, **señalar**, **dar una rueda de prensa**.

**Distance.** The conditional reports what is not confirmed: el ministro **habría dimitido** (the minister has reportedly resigned).

titulo.en: A rumour on the front page

frases.es: El martes por la noche, un diario digital publicó en portada que el alcalde habría cobrado comisiones ilegales.
frases.en: On Tuesday night, a digital newspaper published on its front page that the mayor had allegedly taken illegal commissions.

frases.es: La noticia, que citaba «fuentes cercanas al ayuntamiento», se extendió por las redes en cuestión de minutos.
frases.en: The story, which quoted 'sources close to the town hall', spread across social media in a matter of minutes.

frases.es: A la mañana siguiente, el alcalde dio una rueda de prensa para desmentirla rotundamente.
frases.en: The next morning, the mayor gave a press conference to deny it flatly.

frases.es: Afirmó que se trataba de un rumor sin ninguna prueba y anunció que llevaría al diario a los tribunales.
frases.en: He stated that it was a rumour without any proof and announced that he would take the newspaper to court.

frases.es: El redactor jefe respondió que no revelaría sus fuentes y que aquello era un ataque a la libertad de prensa.
frases.en: The editor-in-chief replied that he would not reveal his sources and that this was an attack on the freedom of the press.
analisis: un ataque a la libertad de prensa

frases.es: Tres días después se supo que el documento en el que se basaba la información era falso.
frases.en: Three days later it became known that the document on which the information was based was false.
analisis: en el que se basaba la información

frases.es: El diario rectificó en una nota breve, pero para entonces millones de personas ya habían leído el titular.
frases.en: The newspaper issued a correction in a short note, but by then millions of people had already read the headline.

pregunta.en: According to the text, what was the story based on?

A false document.en: El documento en el que se basaba la información era falso.

A court ruling.en: The mayor only threatened to go to court.

pregunta.en: In the first sentence, why does the text say habría cobrado?
A journalist who lives abroad and reports from there is…
Complete: the government has denied the story.

desmentido.en: Desmentir: to deny that something is true.

bloques.correcta: the private lives of famous people

texto.en: news from the last hour of the day

traduccion.en: The minister gave a press conference this morning.

texto.en:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (150–180 words).** Write a news story of 150 words about a recent event, with headline, lead and sources, keeping your distance from what is unconfirmed.

**Speak (about 3 minutes).** Debate aloud: are social networks killing serious journalism?
